🚀 Getting Started

Come back here anytime — nothing here is one-time-only

Five steps from a blank screen to a fully working DeltaCortex. Each one links straight to where you'll do it.

1
Connect your market data key
DeltaCortex needs live option prices from MarketData.app — the free tier (100 requests/day) is enough to track a small portfolio. Paste your key into Settings once you have it.
○
2
Add your first position
Use + Add on the Positions tab for a trade you already hold, or tap 🔍 Find Puts to scan for a new cash-secured put to sell. Either way, the card will show its Smart Action within seconds of your first refresh.
○
3
Set your buying power & hurdle rate
In Settings → Trading Preferences, enter your total buying power and your cash-equivalent rate (FDRXX, SPAXX, or whatever your account's money-market sweep pays). This is what every new trade gets checked against before you sell it.
○
4
Install it on your phone (optional)
Open this page in Safari on your iPhone → tap the Share icon → Add to Home Screen. It opens full-screen like a native app.
On Android, open in Chrome → menu (⋮) → Add to Home screen.
5
Sync between devices (optional)
Using DeltaCortex on more than one device? Settings → Data & Sync walks you through connecting a private, free GitHub Gist — your positions stay yours, synced only between your own devices, never through a DeltaCortex server.
○

⚡ Your Weekly Workflow (10 Minutes)

1. Refresh All
Click Refresh All to pull live data for every position
2. Sort by Score
Lowest scores = most urgent. Handle red and orange first.
3. Follow Smart Actions
Each position tells you exactly what to do. Execute it.
4. Ignore Green
Score 60+? Leave it alone. Theta is working.

🎯 When to Close — Profit-Taking Framework

The engine decides per-position, but here's the logic it follows. Profit alone never decides — it's always gated by delta (how much risk remains) and capital efficiency (what your collateral is still earning).

ProfitDeltaDTEAction
40%+ > 0.35 Any CLOSE
High delta = still near the strike. A reversal erases this fast. Target drops to 40% — don't let it linger.
50–60% 0.10–0.20 > 21 HOLD / TRIM
Comfortable distance, time on your side. Base target ~50%, but theta pace flexes it: ahead of pace, hold toward 60%+.
70%+ fast < 0.25 held < 14d TAKE PROFIT
Windfall from a sharp move or IV crush, captured early. Lock it in before mean reversion — unless premium is tiny and decaying fast.
Any ≤ 0.10 ≤ 20 LET EXPIRE
Assignment risk minimal, theta is yours. Closing only burns capital — let it expire worthless and keep 100% of premium.
−100% to −200% Any Any STOP / ROLL
Loss exceeds premium collected. At −100% evaluate close vs roll; at −200% it's a hard stop — cut immediately.
⚡ Capital Override — applies once green
When remaining yield falls below ~2× FDRXX, close regardless of delta or DTE.
Your collateral earns nothing sitting in a near-dead option. The "why" line on each card shows this live — when it turns red, the capital is better deployed elsewhere.

🎯 Health Score Bands (0–100)

The Health Score synthesizes 7 factors into one number. Higher = healthier.

80–100

Healthy

Position is working as intended. Far OTM, theta decaying on schedule, no earnings risk. Action: Do nothing. Check again next week.

60–79

Monitor

Position is fine but has one or two factors trending the wrong direction. Approaching profit-taking zone or delta creeping up. Action: Read the Smart Action. May suggest closing for profit or setting a review date.

40–59

Attention

Multiple factors are unfavorable — delta drifting ATM, theta behind pace, earnings approaching, or IV expanding. Action: Make a decision this week. The Smart Action will say close, scan for roll, or manage actively.

20–39

Act Soon

Position is challenged on most fronts. Likely near or past ATM, behind on theta, or facing an imminent catalyst. Action: Act today. Click 🔍 Scan to check roll viability. If no good roll exists, close.

0–19

Act Now

Position is deep ITM, near expiration, losing on all metrics, or facing imminent binary risk. Action: Close immediately or roll if scanner shows a viable credit. Do not wait.

📊 The 7 Factors Behind Your Score

Hover over any Health Score in the table to see the component breakdown. Here's what each factor measures:

Δ
28%
Delta Proximity
How far OTM you are. Under 0.20 = safe. Over 0.50 = in trouble. The single most important signal.
⏱

DTE (Time)
Days to expiration. More time = more flexibility. Under 7 days = gamma risk accelerates sharply.
💰

P&L Capture
How much premium you've captured. 50%+ = profit-taking zone. Negative = underwater.
θ
13%
Theta Pace
Is premium decaying at the expected rate? ▲ = ahead, ▼ = behind. Behind pace often means the stock moved against you or IV expanded.
📅

Earnings Risk
Is an earnings report before your expiration? Earnings create binary gap risk that delta alone doesn't capture.
📈
8%
IV Change
Has IV crushed (good for you) or expanded (bad) since entry? IV crush accelerates premium decay. IV expansion means the option isn't losing value as fast as theta models predict, and rolling will collect less premium.
📊
5%
Capital Yield
Annualized return on the cash securing this position. Low yield on a challenged position = capital trap. Close and redeploy.

🔍 When to Scan, Roll, or Close

🔍 Scan (pulsing teal button)

The Scan button pulses when the action logic thinks rolling is a viable path. Click it to pull the options chain and see actual net credit/debit numbers. Always scan before rolling — never roll blind.

✅ Roll when scanner shows:

Net credit ≥ $0.30, delta under 0.30, annualized yield ≥ 10%. The scanner's verdict banner will say "✅ Roll viable" with the best candidate highlighted.

⚠️ Be skeptical of rolling when:

Best credit candidate has delta above 0.35 (you're resetting the same problem), net credit is tiny ($0.05–0.10), open interest is under 500 (wide spreads), or IV Δ shows major expansion (rolling into weak premiums).

🛑 Close instead of rolling when:

Scanner shows all debits, IV has crushed since entry (IV Δ deeply negative = poor roll premiums), yield is under 3% (capital trap), or you're rolling into an earnings event. Cut the loss and free capital for a better trade.

🧠 Reading the Smart Action Column

The Smart Action gives you one concrete instruction per position. Hover for the detailed reasoning. Here are the common outputs:

Smart Action Score Range What It Means
Close at $X.XX (+$YYY) 60–80 Profit target reached. Close and redeploy the capital.
Hold — on track 80+ Everything is working. Do nothing. Review next week.
Let expire (max profit) 85+ Far OTM near expiration. Will expire worthless for full profit.
Scan roll — IV supports it 25–45 Position challenged but IV is rich enough to roll for credit. Click 🔍 Scan to verify.
Close at $X.XX (-$YYY) 0–25 Deep trouble. IV crushed or yield too low to justify rolling. Cut the loss.
Close pre-earnings (+/-$XX) 20–40 Earnings before expiration with non-trivial delta. Exit to avoid binary gap risk.
Watch — review in Xd 45–60 Not in trouble yet but delta creeping. Tells you exactly when to check back.

🛡️ Avoiding Common CSP Mistakes

Rolling into earnings

The Earnings column and Health Score's earnings component (10% weight) will flag this. If you see ⚡ or ⚠️ in the Earnings column, the Smart Action will tell you to close pre-earnings rather than roll into the event.

Rolling when IV is crushed

The IV Δ column shows whether IV has compressed since entry. If IV Δ is deeply negative and the Roll Scanner shows all debits or tiny credits, the tool tells you to close rather than roll into weak premiums. This prevents the diminishing-returns roll chain.

Defending positions that trap capital

The Yield column shows annualized return on secured capital. If a $17,000 position is earning 2% annualized, the tool flags this as a capital trap and the Smart Action will say close, not hold. Your capital is better deployed elsewhere.

Letting positions drift into crisis

The Health Score declines gradually as conditions worsen. A position doesn't jump from 80 to 20 overnight — you'll see 80 → 65 → 50 → 35 over days. The declining trend is your early warning system. Act when it crosses 40, not when it hits 15.

🔬 Built-in Safeguards & Intelligence

These systems run automatically behind the Score and Smart Action. Understanding them helps you trust and follow the recommendations.

🛑 Max Loss Stop-Loss

If your loss exceeds 2× the premium collected (-200% P&L), the Smart Action forces a close regardless of all other factors. At -100%, it escalates to Act Soon. This is a hard circuit breaker — no combination of favorable delta, DTE, or IV can override it. The Health Score caps at 10 for -200% and 25 for -100%. This prevents the slow-bleed scenario where you keep holding because "delta is only 0.40."

📈 Dynamic Profit-Taking

The take-profit target adjusts based on theta pace. Ahead of schedule (pace > 1.3) → close at 40%. Normal pace → close at 50%. Behind schedule → close at 60%. The Smart Action shows which pace mode is active. This captures more winners faster and reduces giveback from positions that have already done most of their work.

🔍 Dual-Expiration Roll Scanning

The Roll Scanner pulls candidates from both ~30 DTE and ~45 DTE expirations. The 45-DTE often has meaningfully better credits because of extra time value. Each row shows its expiration so you can compare directly. Sometimes 30-DTE shows all debits but 45-DTE has viable credits.

✅🛑⚠️ Visual Action Prefixes

Every Smart Action carries a visual prefix: ✅ = profit-taking (execute the win), 🛑 = loss-cutting (damage control, act now), ⚠️ = needs your judgment. Triage the entire table by scanning prefixes alone.

📅 Post-Earnings Entry Window

The Earnings Manager flags tickers where earnings were 1–5 days ago with a green "IV crush — good entry window" badge. Post-earnings IV crush is one of the highest-probability CSP entry points. When you see this badge, consider opening a new position on that ticker.

💰 Max Return % at Entry

Each Entry price shows a small "X.X% max" annotation — the maximum possible return if the option expires worthless. Positions with lower max return should be closed earlier because there's less premium cushion to absorb adverse moves.

🏗️ Health Score Circuit Breaker

Hard caps override the weighted composite for deeply underwater positions. P&L worse than -75% caps score at 35. Worse than -100% caps at 25. Worse than -200% caps at 10. Even if delta and DTE look fine, large accumulated losses always surface as urgent.

📐 Position Sizing & Sector Concentration

These frameworks prevent you from over-concentrating risk, which is the #1 portfolio-level mistake CSP sellers make.

💰 Portfolio Risk Dashboard

The strip between the stats bar and controls shows real-time utilization, available buying power, your largest single-name position, and your most concentrated sector — all against your configured limits. Red alerts fire when any limit is breached. Glance at this before every new trade.

📐 Position Sizing in Add Position

When adding a new position, enter the ticker and strike to see a live sizing panel: cash required, % of buying power, available buying power, new utilization after adding, max contracts within your limit, and sector exposure. Warnings fire if the trade would breach any limit. This replaces gut-feel sizing with quantified guardrails.

🏗️ Concentration in Health Score

The Health Score's 8th component (7% weight) penalizes positions in overweight tickers or sectors. If you have 30% of buying power in one name (against a 25% limit), every position in that name gets a concentration penalty that drags its score down. This means the Smart Action will bias toward closing the overweight position first when multiple positions need attention.

⚠️ Sector Correlation Risk

If NVDA, AMD, and ORCL all sell off simultaneously (they're correlated Technology names), positions that look individually manageable become a portfolio-level crisis. The sector concentration limit (default 40%) prevents this by capping how much capital you can deploy in one sector. Configure your limits in Settings → Portfolio Configuration.

Recommended Limits: Max utilization 50–55% • Max per position 20–25% • Max per sector 35–40%. These are conservative for a 5-position CSP book targeting $500/week. Adjust in Settings as your capital and risk tolerance evolve.

📞 Covered Call (CC) Decision Logic

The tool auto-detects Covered Calls (Short + Call) and applies CC-specific logic across all systems. Enter CCs as Position: Short, Option Type: Call.

🔄 CSP vs CC — How the Logic Differs

For CSPs, "in trouble" means the stock dropped toward your strike (assignment = you buy shares at a loss). For CCs, "in trouble" means the stock rose above your strike (assignment = shares called away, capping your upside). The Smart Action, Health Score, and regime guidance all adjust for this difference automatically. The table shows "CSP" or "CC" under each position type.

✅ Smart Action — CC Specifics

CC Smart Actions say "buy back call" instead of "close", "roll up/out to keep shares" when deep ITM, "let assign if target price reached" for positions you want to exit, and "call expires worthless, keep shares + premium" for OTM at expiry. Profit-taking says "buy back and write new call" to encourage rolling into the next cycle.

💰 Capital Yield — CC Calculation

For CSPs, capital yield = premium ÷ (strike × 100). For CCs, capital yield = premium ÷ (underlying price × 100), since your capital at risk is the shares you hold, not cash collateral. This gives a more accurate annualized return for CCs. The underlying price is fetched during Refresh All.

🌡️ Market Regime — CC Entry Guidance

The Add Position form detects when you're entering a CC and shows CC-specific regime guidance. Key insight: CCs are more attractive in cautious/bear markets because high VIX = rich call premiums that offset share depreciation. In bull markets, CCs are less compelling because you risk capping your upside. The regime guidance adjusts delta targets accordingly.

🔍 Roll Scanner — Works for Both

The roll scanner auto-detects call positions and fetches OTM call candidates. For CCs, "rolling" means moving to a higher strike and/or further expiration to avoid assignment while collecting a net credit. The same net credit / delta / yield criteria apply — you want a credit roll with reasonable delta.

🌡️ Market Regime Indicator

A composite bull/bear signal that adjusts your entry strategy, delta targets, and position sizing based on current market conditions.

📡 Data Sources & Fallback Chain

The indicator combines two signals: VIX level (fear gauge) and SPY trend (price vs 50-day and 200-day moving averages). VIX is fetched via a three-tier fallback: first the MarketData.app indices endpoint (paid plans), then UVXY stock quote as a VIX proxy (free plan), then 21-day SPY realized volatility as a last resort. The VIX display shows which source was used (e.g., "Elevated (UVXY proxy)"). SPY data always works — 200 daily candles are fetched to calculate both SMAs.

🟢 Strong Bull / Bull

Strong Bull: VIX < 15, SPY above both SMAs with 50d > 200d (golden cross). Sell at 0.25–0.30 delta. Full position sizing.
Bull: One bullish signal, no bearish. Sell at 0.20–0.25 delta. Standard sizing. Watch VIX for complacency spikes.

🟡 Neutral / 🟠 Cautious

Neutral: Mixed signals. Be selective — 0.15–0.20 delta only. Keep 10% more buying power available than normal. Don't force trades.
Cautious: VIX elevated or SPY below 50d SMA. Only sell at 0.10–0.15 delta for maximum cushion. Reduce position sizes by 25%. Prioritize capital preservation.

🔴 Bear / Crisis

Bear: VIX high + SPY below both SMAs. Only sell on names you'd own at the strike. Ultra-wide 0.10 delta or less. Half normal position sizes, max 35% utilization.
Crisis: VIX > 30. DO NOT open new CSPs. Premiums are rich but assignment probability is extreme. Focus entirely on managing existing positions.

⚙️ How It Updates

Click Refresh All to fetch fresh VIX and SPY data (2 extra API credits). Data persists in localStorage so it's visible on next page load without re-fetching. Works when the market is closed — both endpoints return the most recent available data. A staleness indicator shows when data was last updated (e.g., "2d ago" in yellow over a weekend). The regime guidance also appears in the Add Position sizing panel so you see entry recommendations before every new trade.

📊 Performance Analytics (Performance Tab)

Three analytics panels in the Performance tab help you improve future trades by learning from past results.

🎯 Win Rate by Entry Delta

Shows your win rate bucketed by entry delta (0.05–0.15, 0.15–0.20, etc). If your 0.15–0.20 entries win 95% but 0.30+ only wins 65%, bias toward lower deltas. This is the most actionable insight for improving strike selection. Data accumulates as you close trades.

⏱️ Capital Efficiency — Hold Time

Compares average DTE at entry vs days held. Shows capital turns per cycle — entering at 30 DTE and closing at 15 days = 2× turns, which doubles effective annual return. Breaks down early closes (<60% of life), late closes (60–90%), and held-to-expiry (>90%) with P&L for each. If early closes are consistently profitable, close earlier.

🔗 Roll Chain P&L

Cumulative P&L across all legs of each roll chain. Shows the total result in one card with per-leg breakdown (Roll 1: -$200 → Roll 2: +$350 = +$150 total). If your roll chains are consistently net negative, that's a signal to cut earlier rather than rolling.

📖 Column Quick Reference

θ Pace — ▲▲ well ahead, ▲ on track, ● behind, ▼ well behind. Based on nonlinear decay curve.
Yield — Annualized return on cash secured. Green ≥ 15%, Teal ≥ 8%, Yellow ≥ 3%, Red < 3%.
IV Δ — Change from entry IV. Green = crush (good for short). Red = expansion (bad for short).
Earnings — ⚡ = imminent (≤3d), ⚠️ = soon (≤7d), 📅 = approaching. Green = after expiration (safe).
🔍 Scan — Pulsing = recommended. Muted = optional. Dimmed = not relevant. Pulls live options chain.
Strike Δ% — Distance from stock price to strike. Green = stock above strike (safe). Red = stock below.

🔍 Cash-Secured Put Scanner

Find puts to sell, ranked by a balanced score and checked against your T-bill hurdle.

Enter a ticker and scan...
▸ 📋 How candidates are scored
Balanced Score rewards annualized premium yield, a healthy ATR downside buffer, and distance OTM, while penalizing high assignment delta and expirations that cross earnings.

Hurdle — each candidate's annualized yield is checked against your FDRXX × hurdle-multiple bar (Settings). 🟢 clears it, 🟡 beats cash but is thin, 🔴 fails the T-bill test.

If Assigned = strike − premium, your effective cost basis if the put is assigned. Compare to where you'd be happy owning the stock.

📞 Covered Call Scanner

Best strikes to write against your assigned shares, labeled by strategic zone.

Ready to scan...
▸ 📋 CC Strategy Zones
🟢 Recovery (strike ≥ basis) — Small premium, but if called you exit at or above breakeven. Safe; keeps upside to your cost basis. Best when you expect the stock to recover.

🟡 Income (stock < strike < basis) — Meaningful premium, but if assigned you cap a share loss at that strike. You\'re betting it stays OTM. Best when you want income and think the stock stays flat/down.

🔴 Aggressive / ITM (strike ≤ stock) — High premium, high assignment odds. Effectively a decision to exit the shares for premium plus the strike. Use when you want out and want max premium doing it.

If-Called P&L = (strike − basis) × shares + premium. The bottom-line outcome if the shares get called away at that strike. Green = you net a gain; red = you lock a loss.

Balanced Score ranks candidates on premium yield, downside safety (ATR buffer + distance OTM), and how favorable the if-called outcome is relative to your basis.

🔍 Roll Credit Scanner

Scanning options chain for net credit roll opportunities

Ready to scan...
▸ 📋 Roll Decision Guide
📐 Three-Part Roll Test
Every roll candidate is evaluated against your current position on three criteria. A roll must pass at least 2 of 3 to show the Roll → button:

① Reduces Risk — Does the candidate have a lower absolute delta than your current position? Lower delta = further OTM = less directional exposure.
② Buys Time — Does the candidate have more DTE? More time = more theta to collect and more room for recovery.
③ Collects Credit — Is it a net credit roll? Credit rolls are always preferred. A debit roll can pass if ① and ② both improve meaningfully (delta drops ≥ 0.05 AND DTE extends ≥ 14 days).
📏 ATR Buffer (Average True Range)
The ATR measures how much a stock typically moves per day over the last 14 trading sessions. The ATR Buf column shows how many ATRs each candidate's strike is from the current stock price:

🟢 ≥ 1.5× — Safe buffer. The strike is well outside the stock's normal daily range. Low probability of being tested.
🟡 1.0 – 1.5× — Marginal. A strong single-day move could bring the stock close to this strike. Acceptable but watch closely.
🔴 < 1.0× — Danger zone. The strike is within one day's normal range. High probability of being tested or breached.

How to use it: When choosing between candidates that pass the roll test, prefer strikes with 🟢 1.5×+ ATR buffer. A roll that collects credit but lands at 🔴 0.7× ATR is likely to put you right back in trouble within days. The ATR buffer helps you avoid rolling into a strike that the stock can easily reach.
✅ ROLL when you find a candidate that:
• Passes 2/3 or 3/3 of the roll test (shown in Roll Test column)
• Has ATR buffer of 🟢 1.5× or higher
• Collects net credit ≥ $0.30 per share
• Annualized yield ≥ 10% (green or teal)
⚠️ BE SKEPTICAL when:
• Best candidate passes roll test but ATR buffer is 🔴 — you're rolling into the stock's daily range
• Credit is tiny ($0.05–0.10) — tying up capital for pennies
• Open Interest below 500 — wide spreads make the displayed bid unreliable
• Only debit-justified rolls exist — you're paying to stay in a losing trade
🛑 DON'T ROLL — CLOSE INSTEAD when:
• No candidates pass the 2/3 roll test
• Entire table is red (all debits) — stock moved too far, IV crushed
• All passing candidates have 🔴 ATR buffer — no safe strike exists
• You'd be rolling into an earnings event (check the Earnings column)
How to read the table: Net Cr/Dr = new premium (bid) minus cost to close (current ask). Green = you collect a credit. Red = you pay a debit. Ann. Yield = annualized return on the new position's secured capital. ATR Buf = strike distance from stock price in ATR units. Roll Test shows ①✓②✓③✗ per candidate with a pass count. Roll → button only appears on candidates that pass ≥ 2/3.
